```{r, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", eval = FALSE)
```

`ucdpR` provides a reproducible interface for acquiring and working with data
from the Uppsala Conflict Data Program. Data access is its foundation, while
convenience functions support recurring research tasks such as documenting
sources and auditing revisions between releases. The package treats UCDP's
official download page as the authoritative catalog. Start by discovering what
is currently available:

```{r}
library(ucdpR)
catalog <- ucdp_catalog()
ucdp_search("Georeferenced|Candidate", catalog)
```

## Download or import

`ucdp_download()` preserves the original file. `ucdp_get()` additionally
imports supported tabular formats.

```{r}
file <- ucdp_download("prio", format = "csv", dest_dir = "data-raw")
conflicts <- ucdp_get("prio", format = "csv")
```

When several files belong to one dataset, specify a variant:

```{r}
ucdp_search("Battle-Related Deaths", catalog)
brd_dyad <- ucdp_get("brd", format = "csv", variant = "dyadic")
```

## Versions and provenance

Pin versions in analysis scripts and keep immutable input files. Search the
historical page when necessary:

```{r}
ucdp_versions("prio", format = "csv")
old <- ucdp_download("prio", version = "24.1", format = "csv",
                     dest_dir = "data-raw")

```

Imported objects retain source metadata in their `ucdp_source` attribute:

```{r}
attr(conflicts, "ucdp_source")
```

## Compare releases

Historical versions are analytically useful because UCDP may revise earlier
observations as new information becomes available. A structured comparison can
therefore document data updates or help treat retrospective revision as a
source of measurement uncertainty:

```{r}
comparison <- ucdp_compare_versions(
  "ged", old_version = "24.1", new_version = "25.1"
)
comparison$overview
comparison$variables
comparison$modified
```

Use `detail = "cells"` to obtain old and new values for every changed cell, or
`detail = "summary"` when only aggregate counts are needed. A unique
observation key is inferred when possible and can otherwise be supplied with
`key`.

## A growing research toolkit

The data-access functions provide stable inputs for additional UCDP workflows.
As the package develops, convenience functions can extend this foundation while
retaining explicit versions, transparent operations, and familiar data-frame
outputs. This makes the package useful not only for obtaining UCDP data, but
also for recurring data-management and research tasks built around them.

UCDP asks users to cite the relevant dataset publication and report the data
version. Retrieve the current guidance with `ucdp_cite("prio")` and consult the
dataset's codebook before publication.
